# commitclerk

> A command-line tool that writes your git commit messages. It reads the staged diff,
> asks an LLM (OpenAI Chat Completions or the Anthropic Messages API) for a Conventional Commits message, prints it,
> and commits. Implemented as a seven-module package (`diffing`, `files`, `history`, `gitio`,
> `prompt`, `providers`, `cli`) that is also built into a single standalone ~1 500-line script,
> `dist/commitclerk.py`, with **zero third-party dependencies** — standard library only
> (`urllib`, `subprocess`, `argparse`), Python 3.8+.
> Installs three identical entry points: `clerk`, `commitclerk`, and `git clerk`.
> Install with `pipx install commitclerk`, or download `dist/commitclerk.py` and run it directly.

MIT licensed community project. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenAI,
Anthropic or GitHub. By default it calls the OpenAI Chat Completions API using the key in
`OPENAI_API_KEY`; `--provider anthropic` calls the Anthropic Messages API with
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Features

- **Zero dependencies**: standard library only; a single readable file you can audit before running it on your source code.
- **Git-native**: also installed as `git-clerk`, so `git add -A && git clerk` works as a git subcommand.
- **Title override**: `-m "<title>"` uses your title verbatim and limits the model to writing the body bullets. The most reliable mode, and the recommended default when the intent isn't obvious from the diff alone.
- **Mixed doc+code detection**: when documentation changes alongside code, the prompt names the documentation files, reports documentation's share of the changed lines, and instructs the model to take the type prefix only from the non-documentation diff lines (so a docstring tweak beside a large changelog entry is `docs:`, while a commit that really implements the documented feature is still `feat:`). The note is placed after the diff, where it is not outweighed by the prose it warns about.
- **Documentation-only detection**: if every staged file is documentation (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.rst`, `.txt`, `.adoc`, anything under `docs/`, or a known name like CHANGELOG / README / ROADMAP / CONTRIBUTING), the prompt switches to a docs-only framing — use the `docs:` prefix and describe the documentation change itself ("record X in the changelog"), never "implement X". This exists because a diff-only generator reading changelog prose about already-shipped work will mislabel a Markdown-only commit as `feat:`, and `git log --grep` plus release tooling then inherit the lie.
- **House-style fingerprint**: before writing, a single `git log -n200 --no-merges` measures what this repository actually does — the Conventional Commits types and scopes in use (or whether prefixes are used at all), whether bodies are bulleted, prose or absent and with which bullet character, the median subject length, the trailer keys, and the subject language when it is unambiguous. The result is a ~600-character "house style" block at the top of the prompt, subtracted from the `--max-chars` diff budget rather than added on top. Fewer than five commits produces no block; the language is named only when one language doubles its runner-up and is supported by a quarter of the subjects. Only counts and shapes are transmitted, never message text — scope names and trailer keys excepted. `--no-house-style` disables it.
- **Monorepo scope inference**: each staged file is walked up to the nearest ancestor directory holding a workspace manifest (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `composer.json`, `Gemfile`, `mix.exs`). When every staged file resolves to the same package, its directory name is offered to the model as the Conventional Commits scope. The nearest manifest wins over the outermost, so a monorepo root `package.json` declaring only `workspaces` never overrides the package a file lives in; the repository root is never a scope, so a single-package repo gets none. Files spanning sibling packages produce an explicit instruction not to scope to one of them. Deferred to the house-style vocabulary: a history with no scopes silences inference entirely, and a scope absent from the history is flagged as new. Only manifest *existence* is checked, never contents; no flag, no configuration, no API call.
- **Conventional Commits**: emits `feat:` / `fix:` / `docs:` / `chore:` / `refactor:` / `test:` / `build:` / `perf:` prefixes; imperative titles under 72 characters; bodies of 2–6 bullets about *why*; no emojis, headers, or code fences.
- **File-class taxonomy**: every staged file is classified as `code`, `test`, `docs`, `generated`, `config`, `vendor` or `binary` (path signals plus the diff's binary markers). The class is attached to each filename in the prompt, with a one-line mix, and the rules take the Conventional Commits type from the classes that are the point of the commit — generated, vendored and binary files are never the subject and their contents are never narrated.
- **Generated files are demoted, not dropped**: a `generated` or `vendor` file's diff body is replaced by `[... generated file, +N -M, contents not shown ...]` beneath its `diff --git` header, before the per-file budget is applied, so the reclaimed characters go to the code files. Bodies under 500 characters are left as-is.
- **Structural facts the diff omits**: `git diff --staged --find-renames --stat --summary` is sent alongside the diff, so renames (with `-M` forced regardless of `diff.renames`), mode changes, creations, deletions and binary file sizes are stated rather than inferred. The summary is capped at 2 000 characters and sits outside the diff budget, so it survives when a large diff is trimmed.
- **Partial-staging note**: if a staged file also has unstaged changes, one line on stderr names it and explains that the message describes the staged version, not the file on disk. Informational only; never blocks.
- **Dry run**: `--dry-run` prints the message and commits nothing.
- **Resilient**: transient failures (`408`, `409`, `429`, `5xx`, `529`) are retried up to twice with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring a numeric `Retry-After`. A refused connection fails immediately. A `400` naming a parameter the tool sent is repaired once (the optional sampling knob is dropped, or renamed when the provider says *"Use 'x' instead"*) and resent; required fields and `model` are never touched. `--timeout` bounds each request.
- **Model agnostic**: any OpenAI Chat Completions model via `--model` or `$OPENAI_MODEL` (default `gpt-4o-mini`). The provider is chosen with `--provider` / `$CLERK_PROVIDER` from an adapter table (URL, headers, payload, response extractor). Three entries: `openai` (Chat Completions, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, default `gpt-4o-mini`), `anthropic` (Messages API, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, default `claude-haiku-4-5`), and `ollama` (local Chat Completions at `http://localhost:11434/v1`, no API key, default `qwen2.5-coder`).
- **Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint**: `--base-url` / `$OPENAI_BASE_URL` points the same adapter at Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, Groq, Together or Azure. With a local server the staged diff never leaves the machine.
- **Wrappers**: `run-commit.cmd` (Windows) and `run-commit.sh` (POSIX) check the API key, stage everything with `git add -A`, then pass arguments through. The Python script itself never stages anything.

## Usage

`clerk [-m TITLE] [--dry-run] [--provider NAME] [--base-url URL] [--model MODEL] [--timeout S] [--max-chars N] [--no-house-style] [--version]`

- `-m`, `--message TITLE` — use TITLE verbatim as the commit title; the AI writes only the body.
- `--dry-run` — print the message and exit without committing.
- `--provider NAME` — provider to call: `openai`, `anthropic`, or `ollama` (default `openai`, or `$CLERK_PROVIDER`). `ollama` needs no API key and calls a local server.
- `--base-url URL` — base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`, or `$OPENAI_BASE_URL`). Must be http:// or https://.
- `--model MODEL` — model to call (default: the provider's default; `gpt-4o-mini` or `$OPENAI_MODEL` for `openai`).
- `--timeout S` — seconds to wait for each API request (default `60`).
- `--max-chars N` — character budget for the diff; a larger diff is trimmed per file so every changed file still reaches the model (default `60000`).
- `--no-house-style` — skip the `git log` that measures the repository's own commit conventions.
- `--version` — print the version and exit.

Exit codes: `0` committed (or dry-run printed), `1` nothing staged, `2` configuration problem
(the provider's API key is not set, or the provider does not exist),
anything else passed through from `git commit`.

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+ (no third-party packages)
- `git` on the `PATH`
- An API key in `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with `--provider anthropic` — or no key at all with `--provider ollama` and a local Ollama server

## Privacy and cost

- The staged diff is sent to the configured endpoint (the OpenAI API by default; the Anthropic API with `--provider anthropic`) — on a repository whose contents cannot leave the machine, use `--provider ollama`, which calls a local model and sends nothing over the network, or do not run the tool there.
- Nothing else is transmitted, stored, or logged: no telemetry, no analytics, no remote config.
- The API key is read from the environment and never written to disk.
- One API call per commit; a fraction of a cent with either provider's default model.
